source: Temporary photo-level licensed Hays iNaturalist contact sheets, GitHub Actions run 43083530225 artifact 13885871643; one-day retention. Original photo IDs/obs IDs saved. No photo media committed to repo.
limits: Medium-size contact sheet visual review, not full-scale specimen anatomical measurement.
Photo ID community consensus and location flags are not independent field or herbarium confirmation.
One observed name Elymus glabriflorus is synonym of existing Elymus virginicus under Kew/GBIF; never create a separate card.
No source image licensed for public website use by this report alone.

records.visible_evidence: Good views of slender jointed cylindrical spike; detached spike segments/units and auricle-area photos visible.
records.features_not_verified: Glume arrangement, exact joint/awn dimensions and competing Aegilops species not measured.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Close mature joint and glumes with mm scale; check dispersal units and auricles; confirm wild roadside occurrence.

records.visible_evidence: Pendulous oat-like spikelets and grass basal leaves; some field habitat.
records.features_not_verified: Cultivated oats versus wild oats/forage mixtures and naturally established populations not determined.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Mature spikelets, lemma awn insertion, florets, and cultivated versus volunteer roadside context.

records.visible_evidence: Awned Elymus-like spikes in field hand scale.
records.features_not_verified: Photographs do not support a separate species or verified variant distinct from Elymus virginicus.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Map names to existing E. virginicus and crosslink photos if correctly identified and appropriately licensed.

records.visible_evidence: Bunch of tall green grass and diffuse panicle visible only from a distance.
records.features_not_verified: Images lack spikelet close-ups, ligule/collar, and any convincing wild establishment evidence; one is nighttime landscaping.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Clear flowering branch and spikelet macro, base/ligule, evidence of self-sustaining stand.

records.visible_evidence: One airy purple-pink muhly plume over dense basal tuft.
records.features_not_verified: Single image consistent with ornamental pink muhly, not species confirmation or wild population.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Flowering spikelets, glumes/lemmas and ligule with measurements; exact site planting context.

records.visible_evidence: Moist rock/creek-edge habitat and narrow, somewhat contracted flowering panicles.
records.features_not_verified: Awnless spikelet structure and ligule length not distinguished from other bentgrasses.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Scaled head plus detached mature spikelets showing short or absent awns and 2–7 mm ligule.

records.visible_evidence: Slender interrupted-looking spikes with close-up overlapping green spikelets and sheath/stem junction views.
records.features_not_verified: Second glume shape, ligule and floret details not decisively visible; compare existing Sphenopholis obtusata candidate.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Dissect spikelets and compare with S. obtusata to ensure two distinct reliably identifiable ID cards.

records.visible_evidence: Exceptionally useful Hays photos: small tuft, long narrow panicles, scaly overlapping spikelets, partial collar/ligule, mature branches in hand.
records.features_not_verified: Species boundary versus Tridentopsis mutica and T. buckleyana depends on lemma/callus, florets, ligule and anther dimensions not all reliably measured.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Document dissected lemma apex/floret and mm-scaled ligule, compare the regional Flora's older Tridens muticus var. elongatus.

records.visible_evidence: Two observations display open, drooping, long-awned brome panicles.
records.features_not_verified: Unmeasured lemma awns and sheaths do not distinguish cheatgrass reliably from other annual brome species; just 2 local records.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Awn length, lemma teeth, pubescent lower sheath, plants at multiple independent sites.

records.visible_evidence: Fingerlike branches radiating from culm apex, consistent with crowdfoot grass inflorescence.
records.features_not_verified: Images not sufficiently close to confirm branch tips projecting beyond spikelets, floret details, or rooting nodes.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Scaled full digitate inflorescence and branch tip, flattened winged rachis and rooting base.

records.visible_evidence: Single leafy groundcover patch with narrow lanceolate leaves in shaded/rocky context.
records.features_not_verified: No discernible flowering panicle, spikelets, stem/leaf pubescence, winter rosette or sheath details; complex D. acuminatum taxon concept.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Multi-season habit and rosette, ligule, sheath hairs and flowering spikelets; herbarium voucher if possible.

records.visible_evidence: Single open and diffuse lovegrass-like panicle image.
records.features_not_verified: Crucial viscid/gummy panicle axis cannot be demonstrated; mature spikelet dimensions not visible.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Close-up of sticky/viscid mature panicle axis, spikelets and sheaths with scale.

records.visible_evidence: Small weedy grass with open branched seedhead in disturbed bare ground.
records.features_not_verified: Species identification requires mature glumes and lemmas, leaf glands/hairs, and precise spikelet measurement, not shown.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Ripe spikelet under scale plus floral-part morphology; distinguish other Eragrostis.

records.visible_evidence: Short dense barley-like awned heads and annual bunches shown.
records.features_not_verified: Glume/ciliate margins and hybrid/subspecies-level distinctions not observed; older Flora treats subsp. leporinum.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Mature awned triad, ciliate glume margins, lemma awns with scale, possible H. murinum subsp. leporinum name.

records.visible_evidence: Characteristic pink fuzzy open plume-like seedheads and clumped foliage visible; strong general photo evidence.
records.features_not_verified: Scenes resemble ornamental or managed bunches; ligule and florets not resolved and independent wild established stand not shown.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Floret and ligule macro; independent roadside naturalized occurrence versus planting.

records.visible_evidence: Fine threadlike foliage and flowing pale feathery seedheads above tufted base; compatible with Mexican feathergrass.
records.features_not_verified: Could reflect planted ornamental Mexican feathergrass, and awns/lemma microcharacters are invisible.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Awned lemma close-up and bulbous basal crown, native versus ornamental installation context.

records.visible_evidence: Clear several digitate/fingerlike and strongly curved flowering branches, plus scaled rachis and collar region; good diagnostic imagery.
records.features_not_verified: Exact hairy structures along rachis, sterile/terminal florets and ligule details still need close confirmation; other Chloris/Stapfochloa types occur locally.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Spikelet macro, ciliation along rachis, lemma/stamen differences, ligule under mm scale.

records.visible_evidence: Dense pale tan to slightly pink compressed flowering panicles, green stems and tufted field habit across separate observations.
records.features_not_verified: Thin papery pink-tinged glumes and the deeply cleft lemma apex needed to separate pink tridens not resolved.
records.next_diagnostic_photo_target: Open individual spikelet and lemma tip showing deep cleft, papery glumes with mm scale; compare other Tridens.
